message.content: Work GitHub issue #50 in this repo using the /hq-work workflow (read AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md). Claim with `./hq claim 50 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `bun install` in the worktree first, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 50 --body-file .context/pr-50.md` (add --allow-dirty only for untracked generated files you deliberately did not commit; retry once if the push is rejected with commit_refs_rules), then stop and report PR number and evidence. Do not ship/merge. It is needs:keys: write code with mocked tests and list keyed steps left for a human. Never read .env files. A local test `speak > names a missing api key from a fresh process` may fail only because of a git-ignored .env.local; say so rather than working around it.

content.content:
---
name: hq-work
description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
---

# hq-work

`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).

PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:

````markdown
## What changed
- <what the product can now do>

## How verified
- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
```
<tail of ./hq check>
```

## Risks
- <what could break, or "none">

## Screenshots
<UI changes only, else "n/a">
````

Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.

Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.

Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

I'm settling the design: a new scribe.ts that maps tags to a label, with the service taking a tagAudio dependency. If Scribe fails, I'll keep only the Gemini result as a best-effort fallback, while a Gemini failure still returns 502. Both calls will run in parallel, and I'm weighing whether tagAudio should be required in deps, which I'm leaning toward, along with updating the setup and adjusting the existing "persists only gemini,id" test.

I'm weighing how to map the scribe tags to labels: drilling, hammering, and jackhammer would count as construction, car, traffic, engine, and horn as traffic, and siren and alarm as siren. If no tag is recognizable, I'll leave the scribe key out of the patch entirely rather than casting a vote. I'm still debating whether rustling and fabric should map to handling, and I'm leaning toward picking the most frequent mapped label, with ties going to the first one.

content.text:
PR #192 is open for issue #50: https://github.com/ehewes/durhack-proj/pull/192. I did not ship or merge it.

**What changed** (all in `apps/server/src/features/labels/`):
- **Second label:** each spike clip now also goes to ElevenLabs Scribe, through the existing `tagAudio` call, in parallel with Gemini. The new `scribe.ts` maps Scribe's audio-event tags to the label set by keyword. It takes the most common mapped label, and tags it can't map give no vote.
- **Storage:** `service.ts` stores both labels on the event. The existing `applyEventLabel` turns a disagreement into `uncertain`.
- **Scribe failure:** if Scribe fails, Gemini's label stands alone.
- **Wiring:** `live.ts` passes `tagAudio` into the service, and `labels.test.ts` has new mocked tests.

**Verification:** `./hq check` passed on lint, typecheck and test (3/3). The new tests cover agreement, disagreement giving `uncertain`, a Scribe failure, unmapped tags, and the tag mapping. The rebase on `origin/main` was a no-op. I didn't see the `speak > names a missing api key from a fresh process` failure you mentioned.

**Left for a human (needs:keys):**
- Check that the two demo clips agree with a real `.env`.
- Tune the tag keywords in `scribe.ts` against what Scribe actually returns. They are my guess at its free-text tags.

**Entire trail:** `entire trail show` and `entire trail ci-pr` both said the branch has no discoverable project trail. I did not run `entire trail create` or `entire trail ready`. The issue is `size:S`, so I skipped `entire review` and the `review:pass` label.
